**Altruism and self-interest** — whether and how action can aim at another's good rather than one's own — psychological egoism and its rivals, the empathy–altruism debate and self–other merging, inclusion of others in the self and identity fusion, team reasoning and group-directed preferences, identity in the utility function, the evolution of unselfish behaviour (kin, reciprocal and group selection), and the extent of the self as it bears on what counts as self-interest (ADR-062).

| [CLAIM-491](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md) v3 | No action is selfless in the sense of aiming at a good that is no self's: what is called selflessness, collectivist or altruistic, is concern for the good of a self extended to include others or a group, so collectivism is self-interest on a larger self-identity | The owner's position, from the discussion that raised self-categorization theory (2026-10-28 and 29). Selves come at more and less inclusive levels: social identity in self-categorization theory, fusion, self-expansion, interdependent self-construal. Apparent selflessness is then concern for a larger self. Cialdini et al.'s "oneness" result is its best evidence; Batson et al.'s rejoinder and the risk of trivial truth are its objections. It does not say people are self-centred, or that groups have no good of their own. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-492](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-492.md) v2 | If the self is defined to include whatever an agent cares about, the claim that all motivation serves the self is true by definition and rules nothing out; the thesis has content only with a criterion of the self's extent that can come apart from what the agent cares about | The classic objection to psychological egoism (Butler; Sober and Wilson, [LIT-1683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)), turned on the owner's thesis. "Every motive is my motive" is trivially true and does not make every motive self-interested. "My self includes whatever I care about" makes the thesis unfalsifiable. It is answered if the thesis names an independent criterion of the self's extent, such as overlap, fusion or salient self-categorization, and predicts that motivation follows that criterion and not caring alone. | Active |
